questions.q: What should you do before starting a personal growth journey?
a: Work out who you are and what inspires you
Set a strict deadline for your first goal
Find a mentor who has already succeeded
List every mistake you have made so far
questions.why: Lesson 1 begins with self-knowledge, comparing a plan without it to a road trip without a map.

questions.q: What reality check does the summary suggest when choosing a dream?
a: Be honest about your age and your real motives
Ask friends whether the goal sounds impressive
Choose whichever goal pays the most money
Pick something you can finish within a year
questions.why: Lesson 1 notes you will not become a basketball player in your forties, and prestige alone will not sustain you.

questions.q: What does the summary say about waiting until you feel ready to change?
a: You never will be, so the best time is now
Wait for a raise before you begin
Read one more book before starting
Let a crisis force the decision for you
questions.why: Lesson 2 argues that readiness is an excuse and that growth has to be actively pursued.

questions.q: How does the summary reframe the feeling of being bad at something new?
a: You are not bad, only inexperienced
You are talented but badly taught
You have chosen the wrong goal
You should practise only what you enjoy
questions.why: Lesson 2 rejects the phrase I suck at this, since stumbling is natural at the start.

questions.q: What makes long-term growth easier to sustain?
a: Focusing on the process instead of the outcome
Measuring your results every single day
Choosing goals you can reach quickly
Working alone so nobody distracts you
questions.why: Lesson 3 says enjoying the work matters more than how long the result takes.
